definitions.explanation: A four-character idiom meaning that once you become suspicious, you start seeing threats everywhere; suspicion creates imaginary demons.

examples.japanese: {疑心暗鬼|ぎしんあんき}になって、{誰|だれ}も{信|しん}じられなくなった。
examples.english: I became so suspicious that I couldn't trust anyone.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{疑心暗鬼|ぎしんあんき}に{陥|おちい}っている。
examples.english: She has fallen into a state of paranoid suspicion.

examples.japanese: {疑心暗鬼|ぎしんあんき}を{生|う}む。
examples.english: To give rise to unfounded suspicions.

notes:
FOUR-CHARACTER IDIOM ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご})

LITERAL MEANING: {疑心|ぎしん} (suspicious mind) + {暗鬼|あんき} (demon in the dark) = A suspicious mind sees demons in the dark.

FULL FORM: The complete proverb is {疑心暗鬼|ぎしんあんき}を{生|しょう}ず, meaning "suspicion breeds demons in the dark."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{疑心暗鬼|ぎしんあんき}になる (to become paranoid/suspicious)
・{疑心暗鬼|ぎしんあんき}に{陥|おちい}る (to fall into paranoid suspicion)
・{疑心暗鬼|ぎしんあんき}を{生|う}む (to give rise to suspicion)

ENGLISH EQUIVALENTS:
・Suspicion breeds monsters
・Fear breeds imaginary demons
・Once bitten, twice shy

USAGE: Describes a psychological state where someone becomes so suspicious that they see threats that don't exist. Often used in interpersonal or organizational contexts where trust has broken down.
